root_cause.text: The Bluetooth HCI sync path queued `le_read_features_complete` with only a held reference count that was not sufficient to keep `struct hci_conn` alive until the callback, so the connection could be freed by `hci_conn_del` before `le_read_features_complete` dereferenced it and called `hci_conn_drop()`, causing a UAF.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says the bug happens when “hci_conn [is] freed before le_read_features_complete but after hci_le_read_remote_features_sync so hci_conn_del -> hci_cmd_sync_dequeue is not able to prevent it,” and the patch changes `hci_le_read_remote_features()` to pass `hci_conn_hold(hci_conn_get(conn))` plus adds `hci_conn_put(conn)` in both the callback and error path, while removing the early `if (err == -ECANCELED) return;` in `le_read_features_complete()`, confirming the bug was missing lifetime management for `conn` across the async command callback.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the LE read features completion path to always release the connection reference, including on cancellation.
intent_record.what: In `le_read_features_complete()`, the early return on `err == -ECANCELED` was removed, and a new `hci_conn_put(conn);` call was added immediately after `hci_conn_drop(conn);`.
intent_record.how: The completion handler now always drops and releases the connection reference, even when the operation was canceled. This prevents leaking the connection object on canceled reads and ensures cleanup is performed consistently.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix connection reference management in LE remote feature reading by acquiring a proper extra ref before queueing and releasing it on failure.
intent_record.what: The call passed to `hci_cmd_sync_queue_once()` was changed from `hci_conn_hold(conn)` to `hci_conn_hold(hci_conn_get(conn))`, and the `if (err)` cleanup block was expanded from only `hci_conn_drop(conn);` to also call `hci_conn_put(conn);`.
intent_record.how: This changes the connection reference handling so an extra reference is taken before queuing the remote-features command, and that reference is released if queueing fails. It prevents a reference leak or lifetime imbalance when the command cannot be scheduled.

grouping_result.intent: Fix connection reference management in LE remote feature reading by acquiring a proper extra ref before queueing and releasing it on failure.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix connection reference management in LE remote feature reading by acquiring and properly releasing a connection reference across completion and failure paths.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause: insufficient `hci_conn` lifetime management in the LE read features completion path. They add/adjust connection reference handling before queueing the callback and ensure the reference is released on completion or cancellation, which prevents the use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This is the only pre-fix line showing that the completion was queued with just a held reference. The root cause is that this reference was insufficient to keep struct hci_conn alive until le_read_features_complete ran, enabling a use-after-free if the connection was deleted first.

This dereferences/releases the connection in the completion callback. If the connection had already been freed due to missing lifetime protection, this call would operate on a stale pointer and trigger the UAF described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the statement that queued the LE read-features completion while only holding the connection reference. Per the root cause, that held reference was not sufficient to keep struct hci_conn alive until le_read_features_complete ran, allowing hci_conn_del() to free the object first and leading to a use-after-free.

This completion-path statement dereferences/releases the connection after the asynchronous callback fires. It becomes vulnerable when the earlier queueing used insufficient lifetime protection, because the callback can run on a freed struct hci_conn and then call hci_conn_drop() on stale memory.
